The first paragraph runs long enough to wrap across three lines of type, because a paragraph of one line offers nothing to compare a boundary against. Its second and third lines begin at the left margin, and that is what makes the indent below legible as a boundary rather than as ordinary variation.

The second paragraph is indented on its first line and flush on the rest, exactly as the one above it, and the vertical step between it and the line before is the same step that separates any two lines here. A reader with only the leading to go on cannot tell this line from a wrap.

The third paragraph closes the fixture and exists so that the document contains more paragraph boundaries than it does paragraphs that could be confused for a heading, since nothing here differs in size or weight from anything else.
